findings.title: methods-history vintage files (~26MB) approach GitHub 50MB hard limit at universe growth
findings.description: Each methods-history/YYYY-MM-DD.json is a single JSON object containing every ticker x every method result. Measured on disk: 2026-05-28.json = 26,758,844 bytes, 2026-06-10.json = 25,686,837 bytes, at the current ~6200-ticker universe. These files are git-tracked (git check-ignore returns NOT IGNORED; 28 files committed, total 483MB working tree). Committed retention is --methods-keep-days 90 (daily-pull.yml line 554), so up to ~90 of these multi-MB files can live in the tree simultaneously.
findings.mechanism: File size scales linearly with universe size. Roadmap/ignore comments reference a target universe of 12k-19k tickers. At ~12k tickers a single vintage crosses ~50MB, which is GitHub's hard per-file push-reject limit (not the soft 100MB whole-push warning). The daily commit step would then fail to push that one blob, and the retry-rebase loop cannot fix an oversized blob.
findings.reproducer: ls -la methods-history | sort -k5 -n | tail -3  -> 26.7MB files today. Project a 2x universe -> >50MB -> git push rejects the blob.
findings.impact: Silent pipeline stall at universe growth: the entire daily data commit fails because one vintage exceeds 50MB, blocking ALL state (alert-state, score-history, picks) from committing that run. The 5%-failure-rate gate cannot catch it — failure occurs at git-push time, after the script exits 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Write methods-history vintages gzipped (.json.gz) — they are consumed only programmatically and compress ~10x; or lower --methods-keep-days and add a pre-push size guard that hard-fails with a clear message when any vintage > 45MB. Long-term: per-ticker method-history files (like score-history/) instead of one monolithic per-day blob.

findings.title: Manual dispatch run can race scheduled cron run, both write same committed state files
findings.description: The concurrency group is 'manual-{run_id}' for workflow_dispatch but 'main-push' for the scheduled cron, so a manually-dispatched run does NOT serialize against an in-flight scheduled run (intentional per the Tag 219a comment, to avoid 180min queueing). Both runs use the same RUN_DATE_UTC-derived 'today' and both run detect-changes.js (alert-state.json + method-history-state.json), snapshot-score-history, snapshot-r40rx-history, snapshot-methods-history into the SAME committed paths, then push to main via retry-rebase. The workflow comment at lines 642-644 explicitly acknowledges 'a manual run can race a scheduled cron run'.
findings.mechanism: Each run computes state from its OWN Yahoo pull (the two runs may see different data). The retry-rebase push merges file-by-file, last-writer-wins. detect-changes dedup baselines (methodState/methodHistory) from run A get overwritten wholesale by run B. Because the two runs flipped pass/fail against DIFFERENT prior baselines, the surviving alert-state can be internally inconsistent: next day's detect-changes diffs against a baseline that never corresponded to any single emitted alert set -> spurious or missing METHOD_PASS_LOST/GAINED events.
findings.reproducer: Trigger workflow_dispatch while the 02:00 UTC cron run is mid-pull. Both reach detect-changes; the second push rebases and overwrites alert-state.json. Next run's diff baseline is the loser run's view.
findings.impact: Intermittent alert desync (duplicate or dropped method-flip alerts) and a methodState baseline that doesn't match the committed picks/score-history for that date. Rare (needs overlapping manual+cron) and silent when it occurs.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the manual escape hatch but serialize the COMMIT/push steps against 'main-push' (job- or step-level concurrency on the push only), or have detect-changes/snapshot-* detect an already-committed same-RUN_DATE_UTC state and no-op the second run's state writes.

findings.title: Corrupt method-history-state.json sidecar silently resets to {} (no backup, no fail) unlike alert-state
findings.description: loadState() was hardened (F-SM-015, Tag 187) so a corrupt alert-state.json is backed up to a .corrupt.<ts> file and the run exits non-zero unless RESET_ALERT_STATE=1. The PARALLEL committed state file — method-history-state.json (the 8.9MB methodHistory sidecar) — has no such protection. _loadMethodHistory() on a parse error logs a WARN and returns {} (lines 58-61), silently discarding all accumulated trend history.
findings.mechanism: A truncated/corrupt sidecar (a half-written file from a process killed outside the atomic-write path, or a OneDrive sync / editor glitch on Karl's Windows box) is treated as 'fresh'. The run proceeds, then saveState() OVERWRITES the corrupt file with a sidecar containing only today's single-day history (one entry per method per ticker). The multi-day accumulated trend series is permanently lost with no backup and no non-zero exit.
findings.reproducer: Truncate method-history-state.json mid-array, run detect-changes.js. Observe WARN 'history sidecar unparseable, treating as fresh', exit 0, and the saved sidecar now contains only today's data — prior trend history destroyed.
findings.impact: Silent permanent loss of method trend history (Trend.appendHistory series feeding the dashboard Trend column / sparklines). Asymmetric with alert-state, which IS protected. This is exactly the silent-data-loss case the alert-state guard was added to prevent, but on the unguarded twin file.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the alert-state guard in _loadMethodHistory: on parse failure copy to method-history-state.json.corrupt.<ts> and either exit non-zero (gated by a RESET env) or at minimum refuse to overwrite the original this run.

findings.title: score-history/r40rx-history write raw ticker+'.json', bypassing safeSnapshotFilename helper
findings.description: snapshot-score-history.js (readHistoryFile line 100, write line 195) and snapshot-r40rx-history.js (lines 61, 123) build per-ticker filenames as path.join(dir, ticker + '.json') directly, instead of using lib/snapshot-fs.js safeSnapshotFilename(). That helper exists to (a) sanitize [^A-Z0-9.-] and (b) prefix '_' for Windows-reserved stems (CON/PRN/AUX/NUL/COM1-9/LPT1-9). generate-screener.js reads them back the same raw way (lines 162, 180), so read/write are internally consistent on Linux CI.
findings.mechanism: On Linux CI this works for normal tickers including BRK.B -> BRK.B.json. Risk surfaces if a ticker ever contains a path-significant character (a '/' or leading sequence) — path.join would create a subdir or escape — or if these scripts run on Karl's Windows box where a reserved-name stem cannot be written. This is exactly the drift surface snapshot-fs.js (Tag 219a, F-218b-01) was created to eliminate; these two newer scripts re-introduced the raw pattern.
findings.reproducer: A universe ticker with stem 'CON' or containing '/' would mis-resolve. None present today (verified: no CON/PRN/AUX/NUL files in score-history or r40rx-history), so this is latent.
findings.impact: Latent: a future reserved-name or special-char ticker silently fails to write history (caught by try/catch -> counted as a failure) or a separator char writes outside the intended dir. No current corruption.
findings.suggested_fix: Route both write and read through safeSnapshotFilename() from lib/snapshot-fs.js in snapshot-score-history.js, snapshot-r40rx-history.js, and the readers in generate-screener.js, so the mapping has one source of truth.

findings.title: score-history/r40rx-history mix _meta.json control file with per-ticker payload (dir-walk footgun)
findings.description: snapshot-score-history.js writes a _meta.json control file into the score-history/ output dir (line 210). The per-ticker readers in generate-screener.js look up by explicit ticker name so they never read _meta.json. But any future consumer that enumerates the directory (readdir) to build a ticker list would pick up _meta.json (and any *.tmp.* mid-write) as a pseudo-ticker. The snapshot-* loaders elsewhere consistently guard with !f.startsWith('_') && .endsWith('.json').
findings.mechanism: Pattern risk: the directory mixes a leading-underscore control file with ticker payloads. Code that lists the dir without the startsWith('_') filter is the exact class of bug fixed in snapshot-methods-history Tag 227c-1 (the _manifest-full.json ghost-ticker pollution).
findings.reproducer: Any new aggregator doing fs.readdirSync('score-history').map(f=>f.replace('.json','')) gets a phantom '_meta' ticker.
findings.impact: Low today (no dir-walking consumer found), but it is the same footgun that already polluted methods-history. Pattern-tier preventive flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the _meta.json convention and require the !f.startsWith('_') guard on any directory-enumerating consumer, or move _meta.json out of the per-ticker payload dir.

findings.title: methodHistory sidecar pruned one run later than methodState; cleanup swallows errors silently
findings.description: saveState() prunes methodState entries whose every method's lastChanged is >30 days old (lines 117-132) before writing alert-state.json, but _saveMethodHistory(state.methodHistory) (line 156) writes the sidecar WITHOUT applying that same prune at save time. The methodHistory orphan cleanup (lines 347-365) runs at the START of the NEXT run and drops history for tickers whose methodState entry is absent. So a ticker pruned out of methodState in run N still has its full methodHistory written in run N's sidecar, cleaned only in run N+1 — and that cleanup is wrapped in a try/catch that logs WARN and continues on any error (line 369).
findings.mechanism: The two committed files diverge by one run: after run N, alert-state.methodState lacks ticker T but method-history-state.json still carries T's full series. If the next run's cleanup block throws (swallowed), or universe churn removes T, the orphan series persists and the sidecar grows with delisted/renamed-ticker history.
findings.reproducer: Prune a ticker from methodState (lastChanged>30d) and inspect method-history-state.json after the SAME run: the ticker's series is still present. It disappears only next run, and only if the cleanup doesn't throw.
findings.impact: Slow unbounded growth of the 8.9MB sidecar from orphaned tickers when cleanup errors, plus a one-run window where the two committed state files disagree on which tickers exist. Same repo-bloat class as F-SM-001.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the live-methodState-ticker filter inside _saveMethodHistory at write time (prune sidecar entries for tickers not in prunedMethodState in the SAME run) so the two files never diverge and orphan cleanup isn't dependent on a successful next run.
